openai.sample_unit: mammography screens (9,112 extended-pilot plus 15,953 live-use screens; initial pilot overlaps extended pilot)

links.outcome: Additional screen-detected cancers versus standard double reading
links.effect: Additional cancer detection increased by 1.6, 1.4 and 0.7 per 1,000 cases in initial pilot, extended pilot and live use, respectively; relative increases were 13%, 10% and 5% (all P < 0.05).
links.quote: From the additional recalls, six (initial pilot), 13 (extended pilot) and 11 (live use) additional cancer cases were found, increasing the CDR by 1.6 per 1,000 cases (a 13% relative increase), 1.4 per 1,000 cases (a 10% relative increase) and 0.7 per 1,000 cases (a 5% relative increase) for the initial pilot, extended pilot and live-use phases, respectively (all statistically significant with P < 0.05) (Table 3 ).

links.outcome: Cancer detection, recalls, predictive value, and reading workload in the human–AI workflow
links.effect: Compared with double reading, AI-assisted reading added 0.7-1.6 cancers per 1,000 cases, 0.16-0.30% recalls and 4-6% overall reading workload; PPV increased 0.1-1.9%.
links.quote: The results showed that, compared to double reading, implementing the AI-assisted additional-reader process could achieve 0.7-1.6 additional cancer detection per 1,000 cases, with 0.16-0.30% additional recalls, 0-0.23% unnecessary recalls and a 0.1-1.9% increase in positive predictive value (PPV) after 7-11% additional human reads of AI-flagged cases (equating to 4-6% additional overall reading workload).

links.outcome: Additional review workload and cancer detection at a higher-specificity operating threshold
links.effect: Higher-specificity simulation reduced live-use additional reviews from 7.4% to 2.9% (457/15,953), retaining 10 of the 11 additional cancers (0.6/1,000, a 4% relative increase).
links.quote: When the performance of the AI system was evaluated at a predetermined higher-specificity operating point through simulations, the AI-assisted additional-reader workflow substantially reduced the proportion of cases requiring additional review to 2.4% (89/3,746), 3.0% (274/9,112) and 2.9% (457/15,953) for the initial pilot, extended pilot and live-use phases, respectively, while still detecting 5 of the 6 (1.3/1,000, a 10% relative increase) additional cancer cases found in the initial pilot, 11 of the 13 (1.2/1,000, a 9% relative increase) additional cancer cases found in the extended pilot and 10 of the 11 (0.6/1,000, a 4% relative increase) additional cancer cases found in live use (Table 4 ).

links.effect: Comparing human readers with and without the AI assistant demonstrated a 7% relative increase in cancer detection rate (24 more cases) and a 3% relative increase in PPV.
links.quote: Across the three phases, the implementation of the AI-assisted additional-reader workflow resulted in 24 more cancer cases detected (7% relative increase in cancer detection rate (CDR)) and 70 more women recalled (0.28% increase in absolute recall rate), at a positive predictive value (PPV) for screening of 20.0% (3% relative increase) (Table 3 ).

links.effect: Rolling out the AI system in three phases, from a single-site pilot to a full live rollout, enabled safe deployment of the AI-assisted additional-reader process.
links.quote: The implementation of the AI system consisted of three phases to ensure the safe deployment of the AI-assisted additional-reader process into live use.
